question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$, $X = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}$, and $B = \begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 11\end{bmatrix}$. (a) Solve $AX = B$ using the matrix method. (b) If $A$ is replaced by $A' = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3\\2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B$ by $B' = \begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}$, check if the system $A'X = B'$ has a unique solution and explain why/why not.
explanation:
(a) First, check if $A$ is invertible by calculating its determinant.

$|A| = 1 \times 4 - 2 \times 3 = 4 - 6 = -2 \ne 0$, so $A$ is invertible.

Find $A^{-1}$:

$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -2\\-3 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

$= \frac{1}{-2}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -2\\-3 & 1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1\\1.5 & -0.5\end{bmatrix}$.

Now, $X = A^{-1}B = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1\\1.5 & -0.5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\11\end{bmatrix}$.

$x = -2\times5 + 1\times11 = -10 + 11 = 1$.

$y = 1.5\times5 + (-0.5)\times11 = 7.5 - 5.5 = 2$.

So, $X = \begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$.

(b) $A' = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3\\2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

$|A'| = 4\times1 - 3\times2 = 4 - 6 = -2 \ne 0$.

So, $A'$ is also invertible, thus $A'X=B'$ has a unique solution.

options.A:
(a) $X=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) For $A'=\begin{bmatrix}4&3\\2&1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A'|=-2\ne0$, so $A'X=B'$ has a unique solution.
options.B:
(a) $X=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|A'|=0$, the second system has no unique solution.
options.C:
(a) $X=\begin{bmatrix}5\\11\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) The second system is inconsistent because $A'$ is singular.
options.D:
(a) $X=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) The second system has infinitely many solutions.
